links.outcome: Change in predicted hospitalization risk when medically insignificant inputs and prompt reframings were added
links.effect: Adding medically insignificant variables produced a statistically significant increase in absolute mean predicted hospitalization risk and output variability across all four models and prompts, indicating reduced predictive stability.
links.quote: our results show that including medically insignificant variables resulted in a statistically significant increase in the absolute mean predicted hospitalization risk and output variability across all models and prompts, indicating reduced predictive stability as contextual noise increased.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of LLM psychiatric hospitalization risk scores using synthetic profiles to audit reliability under noise and prompt variation as a pre-deployment auditing practice.

primary.practice: pre-deployment reliability auditing and prompt perturbation testing
